cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine check October's company card statement for HANGS Construction, charge by charge.
First, it reads the statement and the books: 21 charges on four cards.
Next, it matches each charge to its receipt. One was charged twice, and a hotel stay over $400 has no receipt.
One charge is personal: groceries the employee will repay. And a software subscription renewed though nobody approved it.
One charge belongs to a job. And use tax, sales tax the seller didn't charge, is due on a tools order.
A journal entry is a correction to the books. It proposes three, and drafts five requests, none sent.
Last, it writes the workpapers and an unsigned memo for the controller, the head of accounting.

All done. The whole statement, just over $8,300, is coded to the cent. About $1,600 is held for a decision. Seven items stay open, and five requests are drafted for a person to send. Nothing is posted or sent until the controller approves.
